transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-24
Start time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~72 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Jenna Park, Marco Liu, Alisha Nair (Redwood); Priya Rao, Owen Marsh, Lena Ortiz, Devon Kim, Samir Patel (Covalence)

Auto-generated summary (may be incomplete):
Redwood and Covalence reviewed the recent 'entropy surge' that produced cascading throttles in production. Discussion focused on root-cause hypotheses (KV cache eviction pattern + bursty prefix skew), short-term mitigations (fallback routing, tightened autoscaling, higher cold-start buffer), and pilot plan for a hardened rollout with observability checks. Action items assigned for repro, traces, and compliance docs.

Topics:
- Incident recap and evidence
- KV cache eviction / prefix hot-keys
- Autoscaler tuning and burst policies
- Pilot plan / canary safety window
- Compliance and data residency checks

Action items (read out): Marco -> repro, Owen -> traces, Jenna -> docs/pricing, Devon -> residency confirmation

Transcript:
[00:00] Jenna Park: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I know we sent a pretty dense deck, we'll try to walk through the key bits then focus on the pilot plan, next steps.
[00:23] Priya Rao: Yeah thanks, uh we appreciate it. Quick context — the surge hit last Thursday at roughly 04:12 our local time, and we saw a lot of concurrent throttle events, then KV cache evictions, then latency spikes across the inference layer.
[00:39] Marco Liu: Got it. When you say "KV cache evictions" are we seeing full-shard evictions or more of a partial LRU churn?
[00:52] Owen Marsh: It looked like churn, but there were a couple of shards that went to near-zero hit-rate for, like, 45 seconds. So kind of a hot-key blowout plus then a ripple.
[01:05] Jenna Park: Right, and just to set expectations, the hypothesis we've been noodling on is a combination: a short QPS burst where many requests arrived with long prefixes causing the runtime to flush multiple caches, which then inhibited batching and caused tail latency.
[01:22] Lena Ortiz: We did some quick correlation with traffic from our recommendation service — it does send longer contexts for some sessions. There may be a bad sampling of prompts that produced expensive KV lookups.
[01:38] Marco Liu: That maps to something we saw in the logs — a high degree of prefix divergence. The runtime's prefix dedupe handles identical prefixes well, but when many slightly different prefixes come in it defeats dedupe and multiplies cache pressure.
[01:55] Samir Patel: Is that a propmpt engineering issue or something in the routing? We changed model routing last month to spill to a higher-capacity pool under peak, maybe that's interacting.
[02:10] Devon Kim: Slight crosstalk — from sec perspective we also want to confirm none of the surges were replay attacks or instrumentation misfires. We did see a weird pattern of retries from a single IP batch.
[02:25] Owen Marsh: We noted a cluster of retries that aligned with SDK clients on older versions, so there's a client-side retry loop in there. We've flagged it and are patching, but the initial damage was done.
[02:39] Jenna Park: Cool. So short-term mitigations we recommend: 1) add a canary routing rule to route 5% traffic to a variant with a larger cold-cache buffer, 2) enable short-term fallback to smaller chunked responses, and 3) throttle per-client QPS at the gateway to smooth bursts.
[02:58] Priya Rao: The gateway throttling is a little scary — we don't want to break SLOs for paying customers. What's the safety net?
[03:12] Marco Liu: Safety net would be a graceful-degrade policy: if throttle triggers, route to our dedicated small-model path that has lower per-token cost but guaranteed latency, and also emit high-priority alerts so ops can intervene.
[03:28] Priya Rao: Okay, that helps. Can we simulate this in staging?
[03:33] Marco Liu: Absolutely. That's in the action items: we'll run a KV-cache repro test that simulates prefix divergence and retries. We should be able to reproduce the eviction pattern.
[03:45] Owen Marsh: Quick note — our staging traffic shape is usually smoother; we'll need to replay sanitized production traces to get realistic distribution. We'll share those traces.
[03:58] Jenna Park: Perfect. Share anonymized traces and a small sampling of payloads — Marco will use them to run the repro.
[04:07] [00:04:07] Alisha Nair: I'll add that to the shared folder and drop a link in the notes after the call.
[04:14] Priya Rao: On the compliance side, Devon, we need to confirm whether the pilot routing to the dedicated path affects data residency — some of our EU customers must keep token payloads in-region.
[04:29] Devon Kim: Right. For the pilot we can restrict canary to us-east-1 only, but we need Redwood to confirm KMS and HSM integration for the private variant. If the dedicated path needs to be in a different region we need encryption-at-rest and transit proofs.
[04:46] Jenna Park: We'll send the SOC2 + KMS Integration note. We also have an option to run the dedicated pool inside your VPC for the pilot if you'd prefer; that adds work on both sides but is doable.
[05:00] Lena Ortiz: That might be preferable for the EU work — we can scope it in parallel.
[05:07] Marco Liu: From a runtime perspective, another quick win is to tweak the autoscaler to maintain a higher warm-instance floor during known peak windows; that reduces cold-start eviction ripple. It costs more but saves on tail latency.
[05:23] Samir Patel: Do we have a ballpark on the cost delta?
[05:27] Jenna Park: We can provide an estimate — Marco can run a config sweep and we'll share an expected cost per 1M tokens with the higher warm floor.
[05:37] Marco Liu: Also, small tweak: enable a larger KV cache size for the model variant while canarying, and configure an LRU window to favor recent keys. That addressed similar issues for another customer.
[05:52] Owen Marsh: Sounds good. Any thoughts on persistent connection drops? We saw a bunch of connection resets at the same time as the evictions.
[06:03] Marco Liu: Those were likely downstream effects — when the runtime falls behind and retries pile up you get TCP connection churn. Fix the cache pressure and retries and those should subside.
[06:16] Priya Rao: Let's talk timeline for the pilot. We're targeting a safe window end of next week. We'd like a 2-hour canary and then ramp over 24 hours if stable.
[06:30] Jenna Park: Week of 2026-11-02 works for Redwood too. We'll prepare a runbook for the canary with explicit rollback triggers.
[06:40] Devon Kim: Rollback triggers need to include SLO loss, error budget burn, and any unusual KMS errors. We'll require a kill-switch that our ops can invoke.
[06:52] Alisha Nair: We'll include a kill-switch in the runbook and add play-by-play alert hooks to your PagerDuty.
[07:01] Priya Rao: Good. Another ask: can Redwood expose per-client throttles and the ability for us to set thresholds per tenant? We want to protect high-value customers while throttling noisy ones.
[07:17] Marco Liu: We have per-token and per-route controls; per-tenant throttles are supported via token metadata. We'll prepare a short how-to doc.
[07:28] Samir Patel: Ok nice. On the security docs, Devon, do you need anything beyond SOC2 and KMS?
[07:35] Devon Kim: Also want to see access logs and audit trail retention details — how long logs live, RBAC for console, and whether API keys for pilot are tied to role restrictions.
[07:47] Jenna Park: We'll include that in the security bundle.
[07:51] [00:07:51] Owen Marsh: One more technical detail — during the surge, some requests started using longer context lengths and the model kernel selection ended up picking a heavier kernel path. We need to ensure quantization fallback is stable under those conditions.
[08:07] Marco Liu: Agreed — Marco: action item to verify quantized kernel path doesn't regress tail latency under long-context mixing. I'll add a test to the repro.
[08:18] Priya Rao: Are there any known bugs in the autoscaler that could have amplified this?
[08:24] Marco Liu: Not bugs per se, but configuration narrowness — default cooldowns can be too tight if you have sudden spike patterns; a small cooldown increase helps.
[08:36] Samir Patel: We also discussed earlier about client-side retries — what should we advise our app devs?
[08:42] Jenna Park: Recommend jittered exponential backoff and idempotency headers. Also bump the SDK to latest; the older SDK had a retry loop we saw in traces.
[08:54] Priya Rao: We'll push that out to the app teams.
[09:00] Devon Kim: For governance, I want a short postmortem doc that lists root causes, mitigations applied, and follow-ups for compliance. Can Redwood draft a template?
[09:11] Jenna Park: Yes, we'll draft the postmortem and include metric cutovers. We'll also include the repro steps and logs.
[09:20] [00:09:20] Alisha Nair: I'll capture the runbook action items and timeline, then circulate for sign-off.
[09:28] Priya Rao: Great. On the pilot mechanics — can we constrain the canary to a subset of accounts, like internal test tenants and a couple of low-volume EU accounts?
[09:40] Marco Liu: Yes, per-tenant scoping is doable, and we'll add traffic-shaping rules.
[09:47] Samir Patel: Any thoughts about fallback model quality? If we route to a smaller cheap model for latency reasons, we may see lower accuracy for recommendations. That could impact conversion.
[09:59] Marco Liu: Tradeoff. The fallback is lower-context, tuned to preserve key signals; we expect some accuracy loss but within acceptable bounds for short windows. We'll instrument quality guards and rollback on quality regression.
[10:15] Priya Rao: We'll need to see bench numbers.
[10:18] Jenna Park: Marco will attach prior bench numbers and run a micro-benchmark with your sample payloads.
[10:24] Devon Kim: Regarding encryption, if we run the dedicated pool in your VPC how do keys get rotated?
[10:30] Jenna Park: KMS in the customer's account controls keys and rotation. We'll provide the integration playbook.
[10:36] Owen Marsh: Ok that reduces security friction.
[10:40] [00:10:40] Alisha Nair: Quick check — are there any additional stakeholders we should invite to the pilot kickoff?
[10:46] Priya Rao: I'd add our lead of ML infra, Kevin Sung, and our product ops lead, Nora Li. We'll share contacts after the call.
[10:56] Jenna Park: Perfect. We'll also loop in an on-call SE to be present during the canary.
[11:03] Marco Liu: One more note on monitoring: we'll expose a custom dashboard showing per-tenant hit rates, KV eviction rates, and model kernel path distribution. That should help with quick decisions.
[11:19] Samir Patel: Nice. If we see rapid eviction we can trigger a manual throttle to protect high-value tenants.
[11:26] Priya Rao: Ok, let's recap next steps and owners.
[11:30] Jenna Park: Recap — Marco: repro + bench + quant path test; Owen: traces and sanitized payloads; Devon: confirm residency and log retention requirements; Jenna: send security bundle and pilot pricing; Alisha: draft runbook and kill-switch.
[11:50] Priya Rao: Thanks everyone. If we can get the traces by Monday and Redwood's docs by Sunday, we can aim for a pilot early Nov.
[12:03] Jenna Park: Sounds good. We'll follow up with calendar invites and the runbook draft.
[12:10] [00:12:10] Meeting close: casual sign-offs and confirmations.
